simple.meaning: מָלַק (mâlaq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to crack a joint ; by implication, to wring the neck of a fowl (without separating it).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Leviticus, beginning at Leviticus 1:15. The surrounding contexts include offering, altar, blood, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָלַק (H4454) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מָלַק (mâlaq) / H4454 is traced through Leviticus 1:15, Leviticus 5:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to crack a joint ; by implication, to wring the neck of a fowl (without separating it)
definitions.full: H4454. malaq מָלַק verb nip, nip off (head of bird; without necessarily severing it from body, compare Lev 5:8 ) (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic מְלַק ,); — Qal Perfect consecutive אֶתרֿאֹשׁוֺ וּמָלַק Lev 1:15 , i.e. head of dove; compare יַבְדִּיל וְלֹא עָרְמּוֺ מִמּוּל אֶתרֿאֹשׁוֺ וּמָלַק 5:8 . compare Di-Ry. ᵐ5 ἀποκνίζω . I, II. מַלְקָחַ֫יִם מֶלְקָחַ֫יִם, מַלְקוֺחַ, see לקח . מַלְקוֺשׁ see לקשׁ . מֶלְתָּחָה see לתח . [ מַלְתָּעוֺת ] see מְתַלְּעוֺת below תלע . מַמְּגֻרוֺת see I. גור [ מֵמַד ] see מדד .

occurrences.englishText: The priest shall bring it to the altar, and wring off its head, and burn it on the altar; and its blood shall be drained out on the side of the altar;
He shall bring them to the priest, who shall first offer the one which is for the sin offering. He shall wring off its head from its neck, but shall not sever it completely.
